data_provenance: Validation/holdout played rows; 2025-26 archived official injury reports (1,320 games).
eval_period: Validation/holdout played rows; 2025-26 archived official injury reports (1,320 games).

hyperparameters.method: E_inj adds out_min / out_new_min / out_pos_min / out_usage computed from who is absent from the box (proxy for the report). On 2025-26 the same model is scored with features built from the archived T-60 official injury report (OUT/DOUBTFUL).

hypothesis: Minutes freed by absent teammates are redistributed predictably (by position and usage).
limitations: Teammate availability is the largest single pregame improvement available; the real T-60 report recovers most of the proxy's gain, so the gain is not a leakage artefact.

point.result: Validation E_inj vs E -0.225 (95% CI -0.244 to -0.205) min MAE; holdout -0.217 (95% CI -0.237 to -0.197). 2025-26 with PIT report inputs: MAE 4.559 vs 4.755 without injury info (-0.196 (95% CI -0.224 to -0.171)) and 4.548 with the proxy (PIT vs proxy +0.011 (95% CI -0.001 to +0.024)); proxy/PIT out-minutes correlation 0.902.

question: Do teammate absences (injury report) improve minutes forecasts, and does the retrospective proxy transfer to the real point-in-time report?
